problems.title: At least one six
problems.statement: Roll a 6-sided die {{n}} times and write down the results in order as a list, like the example below. Order matters: 6, 1, … and 1, 6, … are different lists. How many different lists have at least one 6?

answer.prompt: Number of lists with at least one 6

common_wrong.feedback: That overcounts sequences with multiple sixes. For example, a sequence with two sixes gets counted twice depending on which six you designate first.
That counts sequences with exactly one 6. Sequences with two or more sixes also satisfy the condition.
Subtracting 1 only removes the single outcome where every roll is the same specific number. You need to subtract all sequences that avoid six completely.

solution.title: Total number of sequences
solution.explanation: Each of the {{n}} rolls has 6 possible outcomes, giving 6^{{n}} total sequences.

solution.title: Sequences with no sixes
solution.explanation: To get no sixes, each roll must be one of the other 5 faces (1 through 5), giving 5^{{n}} sequences.

solution.title: Subtract the complement
solution.explanation: Subtract the sequences with zero sixes from the total number of sequences to find those with at least one 6.

problems.title: At least two sixes
problems.statement: Roll a 6-sided die {{n}} times and write down the results in order as a list, like the example below. Order matters: 6, 1, … and 1, 6, … are different lists. How many different lists have at least two 6s?

answer.prompt: Number of lists with at least two 6s

common_wrong.feedback: That only subtracts sequences with zero sixes. Sequences with exactly one 6 must also be excluded.
Picking 2 positions for sixes and letting the rest be anything overcounts sequences with three or more sixes.

solution.title: Total sequences
solution.explanation: There are 6 possible outcomes for each of the {{n}} rolls.

solution.title: Count unwanted sequences
solution.explanation: There are 5^{{n}} sequences with zero sixes, and {{n}} × 5^({{n}}-1) sequences with exactly one 6.

solution.title: Subtract from the total
solution.explanation: Subtract both unwanted cases from the total to count sequences with at least two sixes.

problems.twist: no ones and at least one six
problems.title: At least one six without ones
problems.statement: Roll a 6-sided die {{n}} times and write down the results in order as a list, like the example below. Order matters: 6, 1, … and 1, 6, … are different lists. How many different lists have no 1s but at least one 6?

answer.prompt: Number of lists with no 1s but at least one 6

common_wrong.feedback: That counts sequences with at least one 6 from all possible rolls, without excluding sequences that contain 1s.
That counts every sequence avoiding 1s, but it includes sequences that also have no 6s.
That only counts sequences with exactly one 6 and no 1s, missing sequences with multiple sixes.

solution.title: Sequences with no ones
solution.explanation: If no 1 is rolled, each die must show one of 5 values (2, 3, 4, 5, or 6), giving 5^{{n}} total sequences.

solution.title: Sequences with neither one nor six
solution.explanation: Among sequences with no 1s, those that also lack a 6 can only use 4 values (2, 3, 4, or 5), giving 4^{{n}} sequences.

solution.title: Subtract the unwanted sequences
solution.explanation: Subtracting sequences with neither 1 nor 6 from all sequences without 1 leaves those that have at least one 6.
